newsitem.title: USA: First Federal says court rules on merger.
newsitem.headline: First Federal says court rules on merger.

text.p: First Federal Savings Bank said on Wednesday that a court concluded that the June 19, 1991, date found by a Georgia jury was the appropriate date a merger agreement with NationsBank Corp would have closed.
First Federal, which has pending litigation against NationsBank, said it was an advisory jury and the trial judge had the option not to accept its decision.
The court also found NationsBank was required to offer First Federal about 1.28 million NationsBank shares.

First Federal Savings said in December the Georgia Supreme Court affirmed a trial order requiring NationsBank, as a successor of C&S/Sovran Corp, to carry out C&S/Sovran's 1988 merger agreement with First Federal Savings Bank.
NationsBank was not immediately available to comment.

The 1.28 million shares would be increased by the number of NationsBank shares in an amount equal to the difference between dividends paid by defendants since December 1991 less dividends paid on all First Federal shares from June 19,1991 to the date of the offer, First Federal said.

The bank said the number of shares to be offered was subject to reduction by the amount payable by First Federal related to employment severance agreements as well as legal fees paid by First Federal which exceeded amounts set forth in the court's order.

Based on the court order, the bank said it estimated the exchange ratio would result in a range of 0.70 to 0.80 shares of NationsBank stock being offered for each share of First Federal stock. It said it was continuing its review and assessment of of the court order, which was subject to appeal by both parties.
